quarterly_data.quarter: MEC results briefing Q&A: Q&A Session for 1H FY Ending December 31, 2026 (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A, first half of FY ending December 2026): the second-half plan reflects points that were not apparent in the full-year plan disclosed in May; the impact of the Strait of Hormuz is not expected to be significant and MEC expects supply and demand for glass cloth to gradually ease, so it revised its sales forecast upward. On profit it expects higher expenses, including personnel expenses, shipping costs from higher sales and depreciation of the Kitakyushu Plant, which begins operations in December; Kitakyushu capacity will be increased gradually after closely examining demand, and product price revisions will be carefully considered.

quarterly_data.quarter: MEC results briefing Q&A: Q&A Session for 1H FY Ending December 31, 2026 (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): sales in China increased on growing demand for package substrates, particularly for the CZ series; sales in Japan fell mainly on the pullback after machinery sales recorded in the first quarter, and sales to South Korea through distributors in Japan decreased on shipment timing despite strong demand for memory-related products. The second-quarter profit margin fell from the first quarter mainly because expenses expected in the first quarter were incurred in the second, plus one-time expenses. For PCB-related products, management said establishing new technology is difficult and evaluation and development are proceeding with a focus on user-friendliness.
